title: Embed Ranker Back-compat Contract for Streaming + Tool Calls
creator: Ava Morales
description: Define and ship a backwards-compatible contract that ensures embeddings + rerank endpoints behave predictably across three dimensions: streaming responses, tool/function-calling signals in streamed chunks, and pagination/error semantics for legacy clients. This ticket captures the PM-level contract, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and cross-team asks for Eng/Design. The goal is to allow new streaming + function-call features to be opt-in for older clients while stabilizing cursor semantics and HTTP error semantics for vector paging and rerank flows.
acceptance_criteria: A documented contract that maps legacy cursor/pagination semantics to the new streaming-first endpoints (including Link header and stable cursor tokens).
A deterministic error mapping table from runtime/internal errors to HTTP status codes and API-level error types for both streaming and paged flows.

Signal conventions for tool/function-calling inside streaming chunks (how to surface tool requests, tool results, and final structured output) with a backward-compatible toggle for non-streaming clients.

Backward-compatible fallback: when the client does not opt into streaming, the endpoint must return a paginated, non-streamed response with identical scoring and ordering semantics within +/- 1 result rank compared to streaming mode.
A rollout plan: feature flag gate, canary with 5% of traffic for 2 weeks, monitor quality/regressions and abort criteria defined.
Integration tests that validate retry idempotency for cursor-based pagination across common failure modes (timeouts, partial stream disconnects).
decision_log: 2025-02-15: Chosen tokenized cursor format (base64 JSON blob with stable id + generation timestamp) to allow opaque cursors that can include routing hints.

2025-02-16: Agreed to map internal transient errors to 502 with Retry-After when the request can be retried immediately, and to 422 for client-side parameter issues. Permanent model mismatches map to 409 with migration hints.

2025-02-18: Streaming function-call signals will use an explicit chunk envelope 'event_type' field (e.g., 'tool_request','tool_result','final') to avoid ambiguous client-side interpretation. For legacy clients, server will synthesize a single non-streamed 'tool' block in the final response body.
tasks: Draft public contract doc and sample request/response payloads (PM/Docs)
Engineering: implement X-Redwood-Compat-Version header handling and legacy fallback path
Engineering: implement deterministic error mapping middleware for embed/rerank endpoints
Design/SDKs: add helper parsers for streaming tool signals in JS/Go SDKs
QA: create integration tests for paged vs streaming parity and cursor stability
Run 2-week canary and collect quality metrics (precision@k, latency, error rates)
comments: 2025-02-14 | Ava Morales: Initial writeup — product goal is to avoid client breakage while enabling streaming and function calls for new workloads.
2025-02-15 | Rishi Patel: Added proposed cursor format; Eng asks for a small canonicalizer to prevent token drift across upgrades.
2025-02-17 | Mei Chen (Eng): Raised concern about partial stream disconnects and the need for server-side resumable cursors. Suggested including a small resume token in each stream checkpoint.
2025-02-19 | Samir Gupta (SDK Lead): Will add parser helpers in node/python SDKs for event_type envelopes; flagged need for clear docs for 'final' synthesized block for legacy clients.
2025-02-20 | Ava Morales: Updated acceptance criteria to include regression tests and abort criteria for canary.
notes: Tradeoffs: opaque cursors ease future changes but make debugging harder — we'll include debug endpoints for support. Rollout will be opt-in via X-Redwood-Compat-Version and a gateway-level feature-flag. Monitoring: precision@10, streaming chunk error rate, cursor mismatch rate, and customer reported regressions.
